subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should OpenClaw add narrow external CDP/noVNC sandbox-browser endpoint config now, or first design a backend-owned sandbox-browser contract with explicit security and lifecycle rules?
rationale: The request changes public sandbox config and browser-control authority, so automation cannot safely choose the endpoint shape, lifecycle owner, CDP/noVNC auth model, or security requirements.

options.title: Design Backend-Owned Contract
options.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit auth, noVNC, SSRF, lifecycle, docs, and tests before landing user-facing config.

options.title: Land Narrow Endpoint Config
options.body: Add external endpoint fields only if maintainers accept a smaller public config surface and specify strict validation, redaction, reachability, and security behavior up front.

options.title: Defer To Broader Browser Backend Work
options.body: Keep this requirement open while the broader browser backend/plugin design decides whether sandbox-browser endpoints belong in that API.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Owned Contract
recommendation.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit auth, noVNC, SSRF, lifecycle, docs, and tests before landing user-facing config.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current and historical signal across sandbox browser lifecycle, backend seams, security defaults, and docs for this decision.
